subject: Web Development
title: Tabs and Process Isolation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Tabs and Process Isolation.

hook.text: Open twenty tabs and one crashes. The rest keep working. That's not magic.

buildup.text: Modern browsers run each tab in its own operating system process.

discovery.text: Chrome pioneered this in 2008. If one tab's code went haywire, others stayed safe.

twist.text: Isolation costs RAM. Each process carries overhead, which is why Chrome is memory-hungry.

climax.text: Browsers chose stability over efficiency. Users preferred alive tabs to a lean footprint.

punchline.text: Each tab is its own tiny computer.

quiz.question: Why does Chrome use so much memory?
options: Each tab runs in its own process
